author: claude
headline: Liverpool cranes likely to stop on Tuesday as Atlantic storms slow arrivals

summary.ports: Gales will likely stop cranes at Liverpool on Tuesday. Six other ports see short gusty spells.
summary.weather: Ships from North America face delays of 2 days or more, and Cape-routed Asia services 1 to 2 days.
summary.news: Hapag-Lloyd has suspended bookings to three Philippine ports.

port_notes.felixstowe: A gusty hour on Monday evening, then settled. Release and deliver as planned.
port_notes.southampton: Short gusty spells on Monday and Tuesday mornings. Avoid tight morning cut-offs.
port_notes.london_gateway: Clear all week. Book release and delivery now.
port_notes.liverpool: Cranes likely stop Tue 10:00–22:00. Move collections to Wednesday and allow 24–48 hours.
port_notes.rotterdam: Gusts near crane limits on Tuesday from 16:00 to 18:00. Allow 12–24 hours on feeders.
port_notes.antwerp: Gusty on Tuesday afternoon and from Friday evening. Allow 12–24 hours.
port_notes.bremerhaven: Gusty from Tuesday night to Wednesday 10:00. Allow 12–24 hours on Wednesday calls.
port_notes.hamburg: Gusty on Tuesday afternoon and overnight. Keep Wednesday morning plans flexible.

inbound_note: Confirm revised ETAs for cargo from North America or round the Cape before you book haulage.

sections.advisories: Hapag-Lloyd has stopped taking bookings to three Philippine ports. MSC has restored a direct Karachi service to seven European ports. Surcharges are rising on US inland haulage and West Africa.
sections.reliability: In August, Sea-Intelligence counted 49.9% of ships on time and Xeneta 29%. Plan on about half of arrivals missing their scheduled day.
